title: Information Theory
dek: How much information a message carries, how far it can be squeezed, and what that has to do with surprise. Written for someone who knows Prelims probability and nothing else.
blurb: Entropy, divergence and mutual information, typical sequences, and the codes that compress a source down to its entropy.
colophon: Based on the lecture notes for B8.4 Information Theory (adapted from those of Harald Oberhauser, Hanqing Jin and Sam Cohen), which follow Cover and Thomas, Elements of Information Theory. Numbering follows the notes. The introduction and Chapters 1 to 3 are here; channel coding (Chapters 4 and 5) is not written yet. The background boxes, figures and exercises are additions; errors in them are new.
